title: Second-lining and the early brass bands
summary: Williams remembers following Ory's little brass band as a boy and describes Excelsior, Onward and other bands that played marches and hymns, not jazz.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Okay, we'll see. We caught you that time. Another thing to do. What about some of the early parade bands that you used to hear? Did you second line much when you were a little boy?
Yeah, I was second line behind Edelmore.
He was playing with... Ori had him a little brass band.
Ori had a brass band. Black Benny was playing bass drum with him. I can't remember all the players. He was with him. He had a little brass band. Mm-hmm.
They liked George Williams' band with Pete. They didn't play no marches, you see? A tunk band.
Did you give my band the numbers they played? No, Paramount, Our Society, and the blues.

And several numbers they would play in the dance band, you know, see? Mm-hmm. Just like we do, you know? Mm-hmm. But I can't remember them all now. Mm-hmm. Because I was quite small, about 13, 14 years old.
Any other brass bands that you liked when you were little? Mm-hmm.

I didn't like them until I started playing with them. I liked Excelsa brass band. They had a fine brass band. Mm-hmm. You, uh, Excelsa, Tuxedo, Armwood, Alan. They had a nice band. Mm-hmm. Brass bands. Now, Emmanuel Perez band, the Arnold brass band, that was on music, you know? See? Marches, see? Mm-hmm. They might play High Society in Panama, but outside of that, they played six-eighths. Mm-hmm. Six-eighths marches and two-four marches. You didn't hear no jazz out of them brass bands. Excelsa, no. They didn't play that. They played hymns like Sing On, like he's playing, you know, see, Over in the Glory Land, things like that.
But for those popular numbers, they didn't do that.
